fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is generic multi-principal-element alloying rather than controlled spark-plasma sintering of ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo powder at 800–1000 °C.

The mechanism attributes performance solely to configurational-entropy-stabilized solid solution formation, omitting densification and uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases that mediate corrosion and oxidation resistance.
The predicted 20% strength-to-weight and 30% corrosion improvements are unsupported by the cited evidence.
The experiment does not test oxidation resistance, passive-film behavior, chloride penetration, or temperature-dependent sintering effects.
The boundary is an unspecified entropy threshold rather than the relevant sintering window constrained by inadequate densification below 800 °C and magnesium volatilization above 1000 °C.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad lightweight-HEA property objective and correctly notes that high-entropy alloys can form simple solid solutions, but it does not reconstruct the target processing–structure–property relationship. The target centers on SPS temperature, with 1000 °C producing high density and oxide barrier phases that improve hardness, chloride corrosion resistance, and diffusion-controlled oxidation. The generated comparison instead varies configurational entropy against traditional alloys under unspecified conditions. Its evidence supports only broad HEA tendencies and potential properties, not the quantitative predictions or claimed causal coupling. The falsification rule is also incomplete because it measures neither high-temperature oxidation nor the relevant electrochemical and kinetic signatures.
